speaker: Doctor
text: Could you describe exactly what happens when you wake up frightened, such as rapid breathing, sweating, or running out of the room? Also, have you noticed any new sounds in your bedroom or changes in your breathing during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do these frightening episodes seem to occur specifically during deep sleep when you cannot remember them, or are you able to recall the dream you were having? Additionally, have you noticed any bedwetting or changes in your teeth grinding?

REQUEST TEST: Overnight_Polysomnography
REQUEST IMAGES: EEG_sleep_study

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of Pyelonephritis does not align with your symptoms of waking up frightened with memory of the dreams; Pyelonephritis would typically present with fever and flank pain. Your description of screaming during sleep, followed by immediate alertness and recall of the terrifying dream, strongly suggests Night Terrors. To confirm the nature of these sleep disturbances, I am ordering an **Overnight_Polysomnography** and **EEG_sleep_study**.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terrors). The history of screaming with immediate recall of the dream, combined with a normal medical history and pending polysomnography results, rules out Night Terrors in favor of Recurrent Nightmares. No further testing is required at this time.
